Kac identifies their mean length as 1/π(b) and their expected absolute f-reward as ∑π|f|/π(b), hence rewards are integrable. Apply the iid L1 strong law separately to lengths and signed rewards. At completed return epochs the ratio converges to πf. For f≥0 sandwich the partial final cycle between completed sums; for signed f bound its absolute remainder by the next integrable |f|-cycle reward, whose size divided by its index tends to zero by subtracting two SLLN partial sums. Any initial segment before T_b is finite a.s. by the published hitting theorem and vanishes after division by n. This handles every deterministic start and does not use Birkhoff or aperiodicity.
